summary: The note introduces Guyana as the only South American nation where English is the official language, while most of its population speaks Guyanese Creole, an English-based creole, as a first language. It places Guyana within the Anglophone Caribbean, notes that CARICOM is headquartered in its capital and largest city Georgetown, and records that Guyana joined the Union of South American Nations as a founding member in 2008.
one_line: Overview of Guyana, the English-speaking South American nation with Georgetown as its capital and a 2008 founding member of UNASUR.
key_facts: Guyana is the only South American nation in which English is the official language.
The majority of Guyana's population speaks Guyanese Creole as a first language.
Guyanese Creole is an English-based creole language.
Guyana is part of the Anglophone Caribbean.
CARICOM, of which Guyana is a member, is headquartered in Georgetown.
Georgetown is the capital and largest city of Guyana.
In 2008, Guyana joined the Union of South American Nations as a founding member.
